ConnectionStrings._comment_DefaultConnection: DELIBERATELY ABSENT so production cannot fall back to a development database. Production: DB_CONNECTION_STRING in .env (required by deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml). Development: appsettings.Development.json.

Swagger._comment: Always on in Development. Elsewhere set Swagger__Enabled=true plus Swagger__Username and Swagger__Password (12+ chars) in .env; /swagger is then behind Basic auth.

LiveKit._comment_credentials: ApiKey and ApiSecret are DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Supply them via LiveKit__ApiKey and LiveKit__ApiSecret in .env (see .env.example), or with dotnet user-secrets locally.
LiveKit._comment_IceServers: STUN only. Do NOT add turn:/turns: entries here: LiveKit's built-in TURN issues per-participant credentials in the join response, so static TURN credentials are always rejected, and a client that passes these servers to its RTCConfiguration replaces the working ones.

Analytics._comment_IpHashSalt: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Supply via the environment variable Analytics__IpHashSalt (docker-compose reads it from .env, which is gitignored; see .env.example). Program.cs THROWS at startup if it is missing — there is no fallback, because a default or empty salt would make the IP pseudonymisation reversible by anyone. Rotation guidance and the impact analysis: docs/dashboard-discovery/PRODUCTION-READINESS-REPORT.md section 2.
Analytics._comment_activation: Staged activation runbook: docs/dashboard-discovery/28-production-analytics-activation.md. Do NOT flip the two Enable* flags together, and do NOT flip either before Stage A has recorded a baseline drop rate from GET /Analytics/System/Health.
Analytics._comment_StructuredLogPath: Unset by default, which keeps the current stdout-only behaviour. Set to a path on a mounted volume to also write newline-delimited JSON that survives a container restart.
